subject: mathematics
question_text: If cosh x = 5/2, then find cosh(2x) and sinh(2x).

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name the formula or definition you use and how you finish.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find sinh x
steps.margin_note: First mark. Rearranged the other way this time: sinh x = √(cosh²x − 1) — a MINUS, because the identity is cosh² − sinh² = 1.
steps.memory_tip: cosh x is given, so sinh x = √(cosh²x − 1) — a MINUS, from cosh² − sinh² = 1.

recall.must_convey: That sinh x = √(cosh²x − 1) = √21/2, with a minus under the root this time.
accept: sinh x is root of cosh squared minus one which gives root twenty one over two
rearrange the identity the other way, minus one this time
sinh x is root twenty one by two
cosh square minus one, root twenty one by two vasthundi
find sinh x from the identity

steps.why: The same identity gives a plus under the root when solving for cosh and a minus when solving for sinh. Which one you need depends on what was given.
common_mistakes: Using √(cosh²x + 1), which is the form for a question where sinh x is the given value.

steps.label: Apply the double-angle formulas
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Same two formulas as the question where sinh x is given. The surd survives into sinh2x but cancels out of cosh2x, since only the squares appear there.
steps.memory_tip: cosh 2x = cosh²x + sinh²x uses only the squares, so the surd cancels there but survives in sinh 2x.

accept: cosh two x is twenty three over two and sinh two x is five root twenty one over two
apply both formulas, the surd survives only in sinh two x
the answers are twenty three halves and five root twenty one over two
cosh two x twenty three by two, sinh two x five root twenty one by two

steps.why: cosh2x uses only the SQUARES, so the root disappears there; sinh2x uses sinh itself, so the surd stays. That is why one answer is rational and the other is not.

insider_note: cosh x = 5/2 is legal because cosh never drops below 1, and here sinh x = √(cosh²x − 1), the identity used the other way round. The √21 stays in sinh 2x; a tidy whole number is not expected.
